summary_en: On 29 July 2026, the Life Insurance Association of Japan said that some user information in its Life Insurance Policy Inquiry System could be viewed from outside by a specific operation. An external security firm flagged the problem. The information is names, addresses, phone numbers and email addresses of account holders, including member-company staff, and could cover about 37,000 users. Policy details and bank account information are not included, and no misuse has been confirmed so far. title_ja: 生命保険契約照会システムにおける情報漏えい等に関する調査結果、再発防止策およびシステムの再開について
title_en: Investigation results, recurrence prevention measures and system resumption regarding the information leak etc. in the life insurance contract inquiry system
summary_en: On 14 September 2026 the Life Insurance Association of Japan published the results of its investigation into its Life Insurance Policy Inquiry System. A misconfiguration gave non-logged-in guest users permission to view other users' personal data. It ran from 1 July 2021 until the system was suspended on 27 July 2026. The data comprised names, birth dates, addresses, phone numbers, emails and internal IDs, covering 27,407 unique people (37,929 records).
